Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১) Which one is the most common organism for UTI?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Escherichia coli (E. coli) is the most common causative organism of urinary tract infection (UTI), especially in uncomplicated community-acquired UTIs. It accounts for the majority of cases due to its ability to colonize the periurethral area and ascend into the urinary tract.

  • E. coli → most common UTI organism

  • S. saprophyticus → important second common cause, especially in young women

  • Proteus → associated with urease production and struvite stones

  • Pseudomonas → more common in complicated/hospital-acquired UTIs

Exam pearl:
“Most common UTI pathogen = E. coli.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ২) Which is not a cardinal presentation of AGN?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) classically presents with a nephritic syndrome:

  • Hematuria → often with RBC casts

  • Oliguria → reduced GFR

  • Hypertension → due to salt and water retention

  • Edema → commonly present

Hyperlipidemia is more characteristic of nephrotic syndrome, not acute glomerulonephritis.

High-yield Renal recall:
Nephritic → Hematuria + HTN + Oliguria
Nephrotic → Proteinuria + Hypoalbuminemia + Edema + Hyperlipidemia

Exam pearl:
“Hyperlipidemia = nephrotic, not nephritic.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৩) Which is a renal cause of AKI?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Drugs can cause intrinsic (renal) acute kidney injury (AKI) by directly damaging the kidneys, for example through acute tubular injury or acute interstitial nephritis.

  • Drugs → renal/intrinsic AKI

  • Cardiac failure → pre-renal AKI

  • Blood loss → pre-renal AKI

  • Dehydration → pre-renal AKI

High-yield AKI classification:
Pre-renal → decreased renal perfusion (blood loss, dehydration, cardiac failure)
Intrinsic renal → kidney parenchymal damage (drugs/nephrotoxins, glomerulonephritis, ATN)
Post-renal → urinary tract obstruction

Exam pearl:
“Drugs → intrinsic renal AKI.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৪) Which glomerular disease is common in children?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Minimal change disease (MCD) is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children, especially in the typical age group of 2–7 years.

  • Minimal change disease → most common nephrotic syndrome in children

  • Membranous nephropathy → more common in adults

  • IgA nephropathy → common cause of nephritic syndrome

  • FSGS → important cause of nephrotic syndrome, especially in adults

High-yield Renal recall:
Child + nephrotic syndrome → Minimal change disease
Adult + nephrotic syndrome → Membranous nephropathy / FSGS

Exam pearl:
“Most common nephrotic syndrome in children = Minimal change disease.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৫) What type of pain occurs during micturition in dysuria?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Dysuria means painful or difficult urination. The pain is classically described as a burning or scalding sensation during micturition.

  • Dysuria → burning/scalding pain

  • Colicky pain → typically ureteric stone

  • Throbbing pain → commonly inflammatory/pulsatile pain

  • Cramping pain → commonly hollow viscus spasm

Exam pearl:
“Dysuria = scalding/burning micturition.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৬) Which is the cause of sterile pyuria?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Sterile pyuria means the presence of white blood cells (pus cells) in urine without growth of routine bacterial pathogens on standard urine culture.

A classic cause is renal tuberculosis, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. TB may produce persistent pyuria despite a negative routine bacterial culture.

  • Renal TB → classic cause of sterile pyuria

  • CKD → not a classic cause

  • AKI → not a typical cause

  • AGN → may cause hematuria and proteinuria, but sterile pyuria is not the classic finding

Exam pearl:
“Sterile pyuria → think Renal TB.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৭) Elderly hypertensive patient presented with anemia mostly due to....?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
In an elderly hypertensive patient, anemia is commonly due to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin (EPO), leading to reduced RBC production.

  • CKD → ↓ EPO → normocytic, normochromic anemia

  • AKI → anemia is not a typical primary feature

  • AGN → anemia is not a characteristic finding

  • Nephrotic syndrome → may cause anemia, but not the classic cause here

Exam pearl:
“CKD → ↓ Erythropoietin → normocytic normochromic anemia.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৮) Administer glucose and insulin to correct hyperkalemia if potassium level is more than.......... mmol/L?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
IV glucose + insulin is used as an emergency treatment for significant hyperkalemia. It temporarily shifts K⁺ from the extracellular space into cells, thereby lowering serum potassium.

In many exam-oriented protocols, insulin–glucose therapy is indicated when serum K⁺ > 6.5 mmol/L, particularly when there are ECG changes or severe hyperkalemia.

  • Insulin → activates Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase → shifts K⁺ into cells

  • Glucose → prevents insulin-induced hypoglycemia

  • This does not remove potassium from the body; it only temporarily lowers serum K⁺.

Exam pearl:
“K⁺ > 6.5 mmol/L → insulin + glucose.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ৯) Which electrolyte & acid base disturbance doesn't occur in AGN?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
In acute glomerulonephritis (AGN), reduced GFR causes retention of potassium, sodium, and acids.

  • Hyperkalemia → may occur due to reduced K⁺ excretion

  • Hyponatremia → may occur, often due to water retention

  • Metabolic acidosis → may occur due to impaired acid excretion

  • Hypokalemia → not a typical finding in AGN

Exam pearl:
“AGN → ↓GFR → K⁺ retention → hyperkalemia, not hypokalemia.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১০) Pain during ejaculation signifies.....?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Painful ejaculation (odynorgasmia) is a classic symptom of prostatitis, particularly chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome.

  • Prostatitis → painful ejaculation

  • Cystitis → dysuria, frequency, urgency

  • Urethritis → dysuria and urethral discharge

  • Proctitis → rectal pain, bleeding, tenesmus

Exam pearl:
“Pain during ejaculation → Prostatitis.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১১) Initially CKD is manifested by.....?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) initially may be clinically silent. The earliest manifestations are often biochemical abnormalities detected on laboratory testing, such as changes in serum creatinine, eGFR, or urine findings.

  • Early CKD → biochemical abnormalities

  • Later → excretory dysfunction

  • Advanced CKD → endocrine/metabolic abnormalities and clinical symptoms

Exam pearl:
“CKD initially manifests with biochemical abnormalities.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১২) What is the usual duration of antibiotic therapy in lower UTI?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
For uncomplicated lower UTI (acute cystitis), a short course of antibiotics is commonly used. In traditional exam-based teaching, 3 days is the usual duration.

  • Uncomplicated lower UTI → typically 3 days (depending on antibiotic and patient factors)

  • Longer courses may be required in complicated UTI, pyelonephritis, pregnancy, or certain male UTIs.

Exam pearl:
“Uncomplicated lower UTI → short course, classically 3 days.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৩) Which is the most common causes of end-stage renal failure?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Diabetes mellitus is the most common cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in many populations. Chronic hyperglycemia causes diabetic nephropathy, leading to progressive loss of renal function.

  • Diabetes mellitus → most common cause of ESRD

  • Hypertension → major cause and contributor

  • Glomerular diseases → important but less common overall

  • Interstitial diseases → less common

Exam pearl:
“Most common cause of ESRD = Diabetes mellitus.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৪) Which is not true about Nephrotic syndrome?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.option1: positive history of pharyngitis or skin infection
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Nephrotic syndrome is characterized by:

  • Massive proteinuria (>3.5 g/day in adults)

  • Hypoalbuminemia

  • Generalized edema

  • Hyperlipidemia

  • Normal C3 is typical in many primary nephrotic disorders.

  • Relapse is common, especially in children with minimal change disease.

A preceding pharyngitis or skin infection is classically associated with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN), a nephritic syndrome, rather than nephrotic syndrome.

Exam pearl:
“Pharyngitis/skin infection → PSGN → nephritic syndrome.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৫) Which antibiotics can be used safely in pregnancy with UTI?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Cephalosporins are generally considered safe for treating UTI during pregnancy and are commonly used when clinically appropriate.

  • Cephalosporins → generally safe in pregnancy

  • Tetracyclines → avoided because of effects on fetal teeth and bone

  • Trimethoprim → generally avoided, especially in the 1st trimester, because it is a folate antagonist

  • Quinolones → generally avoided during pregnancy

Exam pearl:
“Pregnancy + UTI → Cephalosporins are a safe choice.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৬) Most patients with slowly progressive CKD are asymptomatic until GFR falls below...... mL/min?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Patients with slowly progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD) may remain asymptomatic until the GFR falls below approximately 30 mL/min. Symptoms become more prominent as renal function declines further.

  • GFR >30 mL/min → often few or no symptoms

  • GFR <30 mL/min → symptoms of CKD become more apparent

  • GFR <15 mL/min → kidney failure/ESKD

Exam pearl:
“CKD often becomes symptomatic when GFR <30 mL/min.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৭) Which is not a feature of AGN?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) typically presents with a nephritic picture:

  • Hematuria → present

  • Hypertension → present

  • Dark/“smoky” or high-colour urine → due to hematuria

  • Urinary casts → may be present, especially RBC casts; granular casts can also occur.

Therefore, saying “granular cast absent” is not a typical defining feature and is the incorrect statement among the options.

Exam pearl:
AGN → Hematuria + HTN + oliguria + RBC casts.

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৮) Which investigation is done in UTI to evaluate continuous hematuria or other suspicion of bladder lesion?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
Cystoscopy is used to directly visualize the urethra and urinary bladder. It is particularly useful when there is persistent/continuous hematuria or suspicion of a bladder lesion, such as a tumor, stone, or other structural abnormality.

  • Cystoscopy → direct visualization of bladder

  • Renal ultrasound → evaluates kidneys and urinary tract structure

  • CT scan → useful for stones, masses, and upper urinary tract pathology

  • Blood culture → detects bloodstream infection

Exam pearl:
“Persistent hematuria + suspected bladder lesion → Cystoscopy.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ১৯) Two consecutive relapse when on alternate day steroids or within the 14 days of it's discontinuation is called.......?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
In nephrotic syndrome, steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome is defined as:

  • Two consecutive relapses while receiving alternate-day corticosteroids, or

  • Two consecutive relapses within 14 days of stopping corticosteroids.

Important distinctions:

  • Frequent relapse → ≥2 relapses within 6 months or ≥4 relapses within 12 months.

  • Steroid resistant → failure to achieve remission after an adequate course of steroid therapy.

  • Complete remission → disappearance/minimal proteinuria.

Exam pearl:
“Relapse on alternate-day steroid or within 14 days of stopping → Steroid dependent.”

Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.question: ২০) Classic triad of acute pyelonephritis excludes......?
Nephritic & Nephrotic Illness, UTI/Pyelo.exp:
The classic triad of acute pyelonephritis consists of:

  • Fever

  • Loin/flank pain

  • Renal angle (CVA) tenderness

Burning sensation during micturition (dysuria) can occur in pyelonephritis, but it is not part of the classic triad.

Exam pearl:
“Acute pyelonephritis triad = Fever + Loin pain + Renal angle tenderness.”
